## Why This Is Asked

This probes the candidate’s ability to handle privacy/regulatory risk in real releases, requiring structured negotiation and concrete risk-based decisions.

- Privacy risk assessment and regulatory alignment
- Stakeholder mapping and trade-off negotiation
- Phased rollout, feature flags, data minimization, and rollback plans
- documenting decisions and success metrics

## Code Example

```javascript
function isReleasePermitted(consent, fields) {
  if (!consent) return false
  // keep only essential fields for the release
  return fields.every(f => f.essential);
}
```

## Why This Is Asked

Tests the ability to facilitate conflicts with tangible outcomes and teaches beginners how to surface interests, avoid blame, and formalize remediation.

## Key Concepts

- Interest-based negotiation
- Mediation cadence and timeboxing
- Clear ownership and deadlines
- Feedback loop and post-mortem framing

## Code Example

```javascript
function evaluateOptions(options){
  // options: [{name, risk, cost, time}] return bestOption
  return options
    .map(o => ({...o, score: (1 - o.risk) * 0.5 + (1 / o.cost) * 0.3 + (1 / o.time) * 0.2}))
    .sort((a,b)=> b.score - a.score)[0].name
}
```

## Follow-up Questions

- How would you handle a situation where one side refuses to participate in mediation?
- What bias should you watch for during interest surfacing and how would you mitigate it?
